text:
All tests pass.

**Root cause:** `LoopContext.length` (and its async counterpart) computes the size of a non-sized iterable by draining the remaining iterator into a list and adding `self.index` (items already consumed). However, if `_peek_next()` had already been called (via `.last` or `.nextitem`) before `.length`/`.revindex` was accessed, one item was already pulled out of the iterator and cached in `self._after`, but `list(self._iterator)` doesn't include it — so the computed length was short by one whenever an item was pre-fetched.

**Fix:** After computing `len(iterable) + self.index`, add 1 more if `self._after is not missing` (i.e., an item was already peeked and cached), for both the sync `LoopContext.length` and the async `AsyncLoopContext.length`.

All tests pass.

**Root cause:** `LoopContext.length` (and its async counterpart) computes the size of a non-sized iterable by draining the remaining iterator into a list and adding `self.index` (items already consumed). However, if `_peek_next()` had already been called (via `.last` or `.nextitem`) before `.length`/`.revindex` was accessed, one item was already pulled out of the iterator and cached in `self._after`, but `list(self._iterator)` doesn't include it — so the computed length was short by one whenever an item was pre-fetched.

**Fix:** After computing `len(iterable) + self.index`, add 1 more if `self._after is not missing` (i.e., an item was already peeked and cached), for both the sync `LoopContext.length` and the async `AsyncLoopContext.length`.
